translation_en: Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to us: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us: Ma‘bad ibn Hilal al-Anazi said: A group of people from Basra gathered, and we went to Anas ibn Malik, taking Thabit with us so that he would ask Anas about the hadith of intercession for us. We found him in his palace, having finished the forenoon prayer. We asked permission, and he admitted us while seated on his bed. We said to Thabit, “Do not ask him anything before asking about the hadith of intercession.” He said, “Abu Hamzah, these are your brothers from Basra. They have come to ask you about the hadith of intercession.” Anas said: Muhammad narrated to us: “When the Day of Resurrection comes, people will surge against one another. They will come to Adam and say, ‘Intercede for us with your Lord.’ He will say, ‘I am not suited for that, but go to Ibrahim, for he is the close friend of the Most Merciful.’ They will go to Ibrahim, who will say, ‘I am not suited for that, but go to Moses, for Allah spoke to him.’ They will go to Moses, who will say, ‘I am not suited for that, but go to Jesus, for he is the Spirit of Allah and His Word.’ They will go to Jesus, who will say, ‘I am not suited for that, but go to Muhammad.’ They will come to me, and I will say, ‘I am suited for that.’ I will ask my Lord’s permission, and it will be granted to me. He will inspire me with praises by which to praise Him, which do not occur to me now. I will praise Him with those praises and fall down prostrate before Him. It will be said, ‘O Muhammad, raise your head. Speak, and you will be heard; ask, and you will be given; intercede, and your intercession will be accepted.’ I will say, ‘My Lord, my community, my community.’ It will be said, ‘Go and bring out whoever has in his heart faith weighing a barley grain.’ I will go and do so, then return and praise Him with those praises and fall down prostrate before Him. It will be said, ‘O Muhammad, raise your head. Speak, and you will be heard; ask, and you will be given; intercede, and your intercession will be accepted.’ I will say, ‘My Lord, my community, my community.’ It will be said, ‘Go and bring out whoever has in his heart faith weighing a speck or a mustard seed.’ I will go and do so, then return and praise Him with those praises and fall down prostrate before Him. It will be said, ‘O Muhammad, raise your head. Speak, and you will be heard; ask, and you will be given; intercede, and your intercession will be accepted.’ I will say, ‘My Lord, my community, my community.’ He will say, ‘Go and bring out whoever has the very least, the very least, the very least faith in his heart, the weight of a mustard seed, and bring him out of the Fire.’ I will go and do so.” When we left Anas, I said to some of our companions, “If only we went to al-Hasan, who is staying in Abu Khalifah’s house, and he told us what Anas ibn Malik told us.” We went to him, greeted him, and he admitted us. We said, “Abu Sa‘id, we have come from your brother Anas ibn Malik, and we have not heard the same account of intercession that you narrated.” He said, “Tell me.” We recounted the hadith to him. When we reached this point, he said, “Tell me more.” We said, “He did not add anything beyond this.” He said, “He narrated it to me in full twenty years ago. I do not know whether he forgot or disliked that you should rely on it.” We said, “Abu Sa‘id, then narrate it to us.” He laughed and said, “Man was created hasty. I never mention it except that I intend to narrate it to you.” He narrated it to us just as Anas had, then said: “Then I will return a fourth time and praise Him with those praises, then fall down prostrate before Him. It will be said, ‘O Muhammad, raise your head. Speak, and you will be heard; ask, and you will be given; intercede, and your intercession will be accepted.’ I will say, ‘My Lord, give me permission concerning whoever said, “There is no god but Allah.”’ He will say, ‘By My might, majesty, grandeur, and greatness, I will surely bring out of it whoever said, “There is no god but Allah.”’”
